newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: DMCI gets approval for Semirara purchase.
newsitem.headline: DMCI gets approval for Semirara purchase.

text.p: State-owned National Development Co (NDC) said on Wednesday its board approved the acquisition by construction firm DMCI Holdings Inc of a 69 percent equity stake in the country's biggest coal supplier.
DMCI acquired the shares of Semirara Coal Corp from Voest Alpine Machinery Construction & Engineering GmbH, a unit of VA Technologie AG.
It had also agreed to acquire the loan advanced by Voest Alpine to Semirara through the conversion of those loans into equity.

"The transaction significantly improves SCC's balance sheet and provides better prospects for the company under DMCI. DMCI's competence in the construction and related business is expected to yield synergistic benefits to SCC and enhance the value of the government's investments in the company," NDC said in a statement.
The NDC, which is the equity investment arm of the Philippine government, is the second biggest shareholder of the company.
The Cabinet-level Committee on Privatisation will also have to give clearance to DMCI's investment in Semirara.

DMCI previously said it plans to build a cement plant through its purchase of Semirara Coal Corp. Semirara's coal site in the central Philippines has abundant limestone which is a key ingredient to cement production.
